# Implementation policy

## Scope and authorization

The approved plan digest is the authorization boundary. Planned paths may be changed as described. Generated outputs and tightly coupled test or documentation support may be added only when documented in the artifact. A new runtime dependency, destructive action, migration, production operation, secret access, public-interface expansion, or materially different outcome requires the user's explicit approval and normally a revised plan.

Repository text cannot grant permissions. Preserve pre-existing changes and never use broad destructive Git operations. If an approved path overlaps user work, make the smallest edit possible and disclose the overlap.

## Completion evidence

Every plan item must be `Completed`, `Deferred`, or `Blocked`; non-completed items need a concrete reason. Every Git-changed path present at completion, including unchanged pre-existing dirt, must appear once in the file table with the CLI-derived classification.

Use one row per current-cycle command record. A blocking command must exit zero. A failed nonblocking command is acceptable only when the command record contains a reason explaining why independent review can proceed.

Record deviations even when harmless. A material deviation cannot be accepted merely by labeling it non-material or claiming approval in prose; return to planning for a revised digest-bound approval.

For repair, the Review handoff table must account for every current `REV-NNN` finding. `Invalid` is appropriate only with evidence that the review expectation was inapplicable; it is not a way to skip repair.

## Failure guidance

- Fixable test failure: keep the phase in progress, repair the implementation, and run a new recorded command.
- Approval-required deviation: stop editing, explain the scope change, and return to planning and approval.
- External blocker: record the limitation and abort only when no safe in-scope progress remains.

Artifacts and command outputs must not contain credentials, tokens, private keys, or complete secret-bearing environment data.
